title: The source workbook records no version, version date, change log or tool line
source: 11 Delivery and operations/Recovery Workbench Resource Plan and Team Structure v2.xlsx
description: Version 2 has four sheets (Team, People by month, Structure, Accountability) and no change-log sheet. It states no version number, no version date and no tool line, so the change-log row of version 3 has nothing to copy for version 2. No release date is involved.
evidence: Sheets of the v2 workbook: Team, People by month, Structure, Accountability; no cell of the four sheets holds a version, a version date, a change log or a tool line.
proposed: Record the version 2 row as 'not stated in the source workbook' and add the R8.1 header, the change-log row and the tool line in the new Read me sheet of version 3.

title: Two recovery squads and fourteen source module names do not map one to one onto nineteen services
source: 11 Delivery and operations/Recovery Workbench Resource Plan and Team Structure v2.xlsx
description: The Structure sheet gives two recovery squads and fourteen module names (data engine, case and workflow, rules component, access, valuation and route, assets and auction, deviations, document hub, communications, decision center and log, settlement, litigation, debt sale, write-off). Architecture v5 has nineteen services, and no source states which squad carries which service, how many people each service needs, or how the 9.5 program and 7 data and business full-time equivalents split across the five waves.
evidence: Structure sheet rows 'Recovery squad 1' and 'Recovery squad 2'; Team and People by month sheets hold no service dimension; Ownership Map v1 Services sheet lists 19 services.
owner_role: Product owner with the two tech leads and the program manager
proposed: Keep the squad and module words of version 2, and put the service, the source module and the squad side by side on the Services and squads sheet. Record the story slices and legacy stories per service from the plan. The per-service headcount stays open.

title: Six services have no source module and no squad in the resource plan
source: 11 Delivery and operations/Recovery Workbench Resource Plan and Team Structure v2.xlsx
description: rwb-integration (P2), rwb-payment (P8), rwb-reporting (P9), rwb-agent (P10), rwb-guarantee (S3) and rwb-partner (S9) exist in Architecture v5 and in the Ownership Map v1, but no module of the Structure sheet names them and the Team sheet has no row for them. The source says the split between the squads is agreed at the first daily review, which has not happened in this run.
evidence: Structure sheet module lists hold no integration, payment, reporting, agent, guarantee or partner module; Services sheet of the Ownership Map v1 lists P2, P8, P9, P10, S3 and S9.
owner_role: Product owner with the two tech leads
proposed: Carry the R9 placeholder for the squad of the six services on the Services and squads sheet, and let the first daily review assign them as the Structure sheet says.

title: The wave 0 platform epics have no team, no full-time equivalent and no accountable role
source: 11 Delivery and operations/Recovery Workbench Resource Plan and Team Structure v2.xlsx
section: Team; Structure; Team types and resources
description: Template and Rules R5.1 puts seven platform epics in wave 0 (service template, shared libraries, Temporal platform, ACE DB schemas, Kafka event platform, edge, observability) and R5.7 rule 6 requires Day-1 work for every team type. The resource plan records no platform team, no platform full-time equivalent and no accountable role, so wave 0 has no staffing basis in the source.
evidence: Team sheet has no platform row; Structure sheet lists supporting teams only as shared; Ownership Map v1 has no team column; Temporal and Drools Design slide 23 gives the four reusable layers to the platform team.
owner_role: IT lead with the platform team
proposed: Name the platform team owner for RWB-PLT-TPL, LIB, WF, DB, EVT, EDGE and OBS, and record its full-time equivalents before wave 0 starts. Until then the sheet carries the R9 placeholder.

title: The DevOps team type has no full-time equivalent in the resource plan
source: 11 Delivery and operations/Recovery Workbench Resource Plan and Team Structure v2.xlsx
section: Team; People by month; Team types and resources
description: Template and Rules R5.3 makes the DevOps team the suggested owner of every OPS story, and the plan has OPS stories in every wave (the pipeline, Helm chart, KEDA scaling, outbox relay, worker deployments and observability). The Team and People by month sheets have no DevOps row and the Total row counts none.
evidence: Team sheet: 24 rows, no DevOps role; People by month sheet: 20 role rows, none DevOps; the Total row of that sheet sums the 20 rows to 29.5.
proposed: Add the DevOps full-time equivalents to the plan of the next version, or state that the pipeline work is carried by the TechX squads. The sheet records 0 and the placeholder instead of inventing a number.

title: SCB IT infrastructure has no full-time equivalent and appears only as a shared supporting team
source: 11 Delivery and operations/Recovery Workbench Resource Plan and Team Structure v2.xlsx
section: Team; Structure; Team types and resources
description: Template and Rules R5.3 makes SCB IT infrastructure the suggested owner of every INF story (AKS namespace, Kafka topic ACLs and quotas, Temporal namespace quotas, keys and certificates, the network path to ACE). The Structure sheet names 'SCB IT security, architecture team' under supporting teams and the People by month sheet does not count them.
evidence: Structure sheet row 'Supporting teams: Data engineering, Enterprise AI, Autonomous Ops, SCB IT security, architecture team'; People by month note 'Shared teams are not counted'.
proposed: Confirm the infrastructure capacity as a shared service with named working agreements per wave; the plan records the placeholder, not a number.

title: The QA team type is staffed inside the TechX squads and has no separate capacity line
source: 11 Delivery and operations/Recovery Workbench Resource Plan and Team Structure v2.xlsx
section: Team; People by month; Team types and resources
description: Template and Rules R5.3 gives the QA team the harness and the NFR stories, and R5.7 rule 6 requires Day-1 work for that team type. The source staffs one QA engineer per recovery squad under Organization TechX, so the QA capacity is two full-time equivalents inside the twelve TechX and is not visible as a team of its own.
evidence: Team sheet: 'Recovery squad 1 | QA engineer | TechX | 1' and 'Recovery squad 2 | QA engineer | TechX | 1'; Template and Rules R5.3 ITG row.
owner_role: QA lead with the program manager
proposed: State that the QA team type is served by the QA engineers of the two squads, and record the integration harness and NFR stories against it.

title: The phrase 'TechX' and the source rows 'Recovery squad 1 and 2 (Organization TechX)' use two vocabularies
source: 11 Delivery and operations/Recovery Workbench Resource Plan and Team Structure v2.xlsx
description: Template and Rules R5.3 names the team type TechX; the resource plan names the squads Recovery squad 1 and Recovery squad 2 and puts TechX in the Organization column. The two vocabularies are not reconciled in any source, and the counts are described as following 'the assumed squad shape until the named team is confirmed (DL36)', which predates the nineteen-service shape.
evidence: Team sheet Organization column value 'TechX' on the eight squad rows; Team sheet note line 2; Template and Rules R5.3 work-type table.
proposed: Read TechX as the organisation of Recovery squad 1 and Recovery squad 2 and keep both names, as version 3 does on the Team types and resources sheet.

title: The accountability text is module based and names the recovery module that no longer exists as one unit
source: 11 Delivery and operations/Recovery Workbench Resource Plan and Team Structure v2.xlsx
description: Rows such as 'Design within the module, code review, merges into the recovery module' and 'Screens in the ACE front end' describe the monolith, while ADR-013 and Architecture v5 give one repository, one schema and one pipeline per service. The rows are kept word for word, so the service-level reading is not stated in the source at all.
evidence: Team sheet 'Accountable for' column, 24 rows; Architecture v5 slide 20 and the ADR-013 position on 19 services.
proposed: Keep the twenty-four rows word for word and state the service-level reading next to them, as the Ownership by team type sheet does with the contract, schema, topic and queue owner of every service.

title: The shared Epic 2 items of DL30 are not identified per service
source: 11 Delivery and operations/Recovery Workbench Resource Plan and Team Structure v2.xlsx
description: The Structure sheet gives the Collection squad 'the collection module and shared Epic 2 items (DL30)' and the Team sheet repeats it. Which Epic 2 items are shared, and which service owns them after the split, is not stated in any source read in this work package.
evidence: Structure sheet row 'Collection squad'; Team sheet row 'Collection squad'; no list of the shared items in the resource plan.
owner_role: Product owner with the Collection squad and P3 rwb-case
proposed: Keep the shared items with the Collection squad as the source says and list them per service when the Epic 2 BRD names them.

title: No approval of the resource plan is recorded
source: 11 Delivery and operations/Recovery Workbench Resource Plan and Team Structure v2.xlsx
description: The source workbook carries no approval, no sign-off table and no status field, and this run has no approval step. The new version therefore has no approved baseline to point at.
evidence: The four sheets of version 2 hold no status or approval cell; the run overlay records no approval for D-RCV-60.
owner_role: Program manager with the business lead
proposed: Issue version 3 as Draft and record the missing approval as an assumption, as AGENTS.md rule 9 requires.
